newsitem.title: INDIA: India communists oppose divestment in condom firm.
newsitem.headline: India communists oppose divestment in condom firm.

text.p: India's main communist party said on Tuesday it opposed the planned privatisation of a state-owned condom firm, saying it could upset the country's badly-needed family programme.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted E. Balanandan, president of the trade union of the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), as asking the government to shelve its move to disinvest a 74 percent stake in Hindustan Latex Ltd.
The CPI-M is a key member of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 15-party United Front alliance.
India heavily subsidises the popular "Nirodh" condom made by the firm, seen as a successful symbol of the country's otherwise faltering family planning effort.

Balanandan said he feared prices of condoms would rise steeply if private investors took over Hindustan Latex, adversely affecting the government's plans to slow the growth of the population in India, currently estimated at 930 million.
